speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a longstanding pruritic rash and numbness tingling in your palms. To narrow this down, have you noticed any specific pattern on the skin, such as small bumps or scaling, and does the sensation worsen at night?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That occupational history is significant; have you noticed any blistering, scaling, or specific color changes in the rash, and do you have any joint pain or swelling? I also need to know if you have been exposed to any new chemicals or plants besides the rice and livestock.

REQUEST TEST: CBC, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, Liver Function Tests, Vitamin B12, and Folate levels.
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology photos of the rash on the upper body and face.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your occupation on a rice farm and the combination of a pruritic rash on your upper body and face with numbness/tingling in your palms, do you have any difficulty urinating, erectile dysfunction, or a feeling of fullness in your upper abdomen? Also, have you noticed any darkening of the skin or a sweet, musty odor to your sweat or breath?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Renal Function Panel, and Skin Swab for fungal cultures.

speaker: Doctor
text: The negative workup for diabetes, liver disease, and fungal infections, combined with your rice farming occupation and symptoms of facial rash with pruritus, numbness, and tingling in the palms, strongly suggests a diagnosis of Porphyria Cutanea Tarda. Do you notice any thinning of the skin, easy bruising, or blistering on your hands or face? REQUEST TEST: Uroporphyrin level; REQUEST IMAGES: Close-up photos of the rash showing blistering or scarring.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Uroporphyrin level: Elevated; Dermatology photos show thinning of the skin, easy bruising, and blistering on the hands and face.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Porphyria Cutanea Tarda. The elevated uroporphyrin levels combined with blistering, skin thinning, and your history of rice farming (potential arsenic exposure) confirm this diagnosis. I recommend avoiding alcohol and checking for Hepatitis C or Hemochromatosis as secondary factors.
